title: Leftward sweep span
statement: Let $A$ and $Q$ be types, let $x$ and $w$ be finite words over $A$, let $M$ be a one-work-tape Turing machine, and let $s:	ext{Fin}(|w|+1)\to Q$ be a state sequence. Suppose that for every $i<|w|$ and every input and scanned work symbol, the transition from state $s(i)$ is the action that writes $w_i$ and moves the work head one cell left, entering state $s(i+1)$. For any input-head position $p$, output word $o$, integer $z$, zipper lists $l,r$, and natural number $n\le |w|$, after $n$ steps from the backward-sweep configuration with state $s(0)$ and frontier $z$, the machine is in state $s(n)$ with frontier $z-n$ and zipper lists $\operatorname{reverse}(\operatorname{map}(w[0:n],\mathrm{some}))\mathbin{++}l$ and $r$ with its first $n$ entries removed; throughout these steps the work-head position lies in $[z-n,z]$.
hypotheses_covered: $A,Q$ are types; $x,w$ are finite words over $A.
A state sequence is specified for indices $0$ through $|w|$.
For every $i<|w|$ and every input and scanned work symbol, the transition from state $s(i)$ writes $w_i$, moves left, and enters $s(i+1)$.
An input-head position, output word, integer frontier, and zipper lists are given.
